task.description:
PR #691's CI (mix letflow.check, which shells out to plain `mix test` -- a single, non-partitioned BEAM process, confirmed by reading lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex) failed on ONE of its two duplicate CI runs (run 33165402662, 21m39s, 9 failures) while the other passed cleanly (run 33165423753, 5m3s, 0 failures) on the IDENTICAL commit. Real, structurally-confirmed root cause (not a guess): this branch's own tests (test/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout_test.exs and test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs's new REQ-170 describe blocks) each dispatch a genuinely-hanging guest (req170_hang.wat / req165_hang.wat) through the REAL PluginInterface.invoke -> PluginHandler.handle_node -> Wasmex.start_link/1 entry point. Per this requirement's OWN design doc finding (lib/letflow/design/req170-wasm-wallclock-timeout.md section 1.1-1.4, independently reproduced by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and SECURITY-REVIEWER), a genuinely-hung wasmex call is NEVER interrupted -- it permanently occupies one thread of wasmex's shared, node-global, CPU-count-sized Tokio native worker pool, with NO BEAM-side mechanism able to reclaim it. Counted directly: call_timeout_test.exs's AC2 test (1 leak, same pid reused for 2 calls so only 1 native thread lost) plus its AC5 describe block's two live-hang tests (2 more leaks) = 3; plugin_handler_test.exs's AC5 outer-timeout test (1 leak), REQ-170 AC1 test (1 leak), REQ-170 AC3 test (1 leak), and REQ-170 AC4's two tests (2 more leaks, since build_context.() creates a fresh PluginInterface.invoke -> fresh Wasmex.start_link per call) = 5. Total: ~8 permanently-leaked native threads accumulate over the course of ONE sequential `mix test` run, before later, unrelated WASM test files (module_registry_test.exs, which also creates real wasmex instances) run in the SAME OS process -- exhausting the shared pool on a CI runner with as few as 2-4 available cores causes exactly the cascading failure observed (module_registry_test.exs tests 6-9 all failed/timed out with the pool exhausted).

This is the SAME hazard class the design doc's own section 1.5/section 8 already found and filed as OQ-5-adjacent evidence, just manifesting for real in CI at a smaller scale (8 leaks, not 32) because CI's runner has far fewer cores than the design session's own host. Reduce the total genuine-hang footprint of these two test files to the minimum necessary to still prove every acceptance criterion, without weakening any AC's actual coverage.

Key lever: classify/1 (Letflow.Engine.Wasm.CallTimeout) is a PURE function over an already-completed Letflow.Engine.PluginInterface.outcome() value (a plain term, per design section 4.2) -- it does not require a live hang to test. call_timeout_test.exs's existing pure test (line 165-169, 'classify/1's own two substrings never appear in a fuel-exhaustion reason string') already demonstrates this pattern. Wherever a test's ONLY purpose is proving classify/1's own logic (not proving PluginInterface/PluginHandler actually PRODUCE that exact string live), prefer a synthetic/constructed outcome() value over a real hang -- but keep AT LEAST ONE live, end-to-end proof per distinct mechanism (design's own testing philosophy establishes real coverage matters, per req168/169/170's own precedent of testing real behavior, not just pure logic in isolation) so the suite still proves the real strings genuinely match.

Second lever: where multiple elapsed-time proofs are needed against different timeout_ms values (REQ-170 AC4), choose values that simultaneously prove MULTIPLE things in one fewer call -- e.g., a single pair (300ms, 7000ms) instead of three separate calls (300ms, 2000ms, 7000ms) can prove BOTH 'shorter binds sooner' AND 'timeout_ms is not silently dropped/defaulting to wasmex's hardcoded 5000ms' in one test with 2 leaks instead of two tests with 3 leaks total.

Do NOT weaken or remove the honesty-clause tests (the ones asserting the REAL, live-verified behavior per design section 1.1-1.6) -- those are load-bearing for this requirement's own credibility and must keep at least minimal live coverage. Do NOT modify lib/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout.ex or lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex -- this is a test-file-only fix.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce the total count of genuinely-hanging (permanently native-thread-leaking) wasmex calls across call_timeout_test.exs and plugin_handler_test.exs to a smaller number than today's ~8 -- target roughly half or fewer, while every one of REQ-170's 7 real acceptance criteria (docs/requirements.yaml) still has at least one live, end-to-end test proving the real mechanism works, not merely a pure/synthetic test standing in for all coverage of that AC.

Where a test's assertion is purely about classify/1's own string-matching logic (not about proving PluginInterface/PluginHandler produce that string for real), convert it to a synthetic outcome() value -- no live Wasmex call, no leak -- following the existing pure-test precedent already in the file (line 165-169).

Where AC4's multiple timeout_ms values are tested, consolidate to the minimum number of live calls that still proves both 'shorter binds sooner' and 'timeout_ms is not silently dropped to wasmex's 5000ms default' (a single well-chosen pair should suffice instead of three separate calls).
Re-run mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/ locally (export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH", WASMEX_BUILD=true) and confirm all tests still pass with real output quoted.

Re-run the FULL suite (mix test, not scripts/test_parallel.sh -- match CI's own invocation exactly) at least once locally to sanity-check the reduced leak footprint doesn't still cause cascading failures on this host, real output quoted.
mix letflow.lint_handoffs passes with 0 new violations.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish.

result.summary: Reduced the genuine-hang footprint of test/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout_test.exs and test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs's REQ-170 blocks without modifying call_timeout.ex or plugin_handler.ex. Two changes: (1) call_timeout_test.exs's AC5 describe block -- the first test (inner wasmex-level timeout_ms=300 hang, classify() check) was converted to a synthetic outcome() value, a reason string captured verbatim from one real live run of that exact call shape (scratch/req170_capture_outcome.exs, git-ignored). This mechanism (inner GenServer.call timeout -> PluginInterface {:exit, reason} -> classify/1) is still proven live elsewhere: plugin_handler_test.exs's 'REQ-170 AC1' test exercises the identical shape and also asserts CallTimeout.classify(result) == :wall_clock_timeout. The block's second test (outer Task.yield/2 timeout shape -> classify()) was KEPT live: it is the only live end-to-end proof that classify/1 recognizes the outer-timeout string (plugin_handler_test.exs's AC3 test exercises the same outer boundary but never calls classify/1). (2) plugin_handler_test.exs's 'REQ-170 AC4' describe block: consolidated 2 tests / 3 live calls (300ms, 2_000ms, 7_000ms) into 1 test / 2 live calls (300ms, 7_000ms) -- a pair straddling wasmex's own hardcoded 5_000ms default proves both 'shorter binds sooner' and 'timeout_ms is not silently dropped to the hardcoded default' (M6's own mutation-guard concern, per test/specs/REQ-170.md) in the minimum number of calls. AC1, AC2, AC3, and REQ-165's own pre-existing AC5 outer-timeout test were left untouched -- each is the sole live end-to-end proof of a distinct mechanism, so touching them would have weakened real coverage for its own AC.

leak_count.before: ~8-9 genuinely-hanging (permanently native-thread-leaking) live wasmex calls across the two files (call_timeout_test.exs: AC2's direct Wasmex.call_function/4 test = 1, AC5's two live-hang tests = 2, total 3; plugin_handler_test.exs: REQ-165's own pre-existing AC5 outer-timeout test = 1, REQ-170 AC1 = 1, REQ-170 AC3 = 1, REQ-170 AC4's two tests = 3 live calls [300ms+2_000ms in test 1, 7_000ms in test 2], total 6; grand total 3+6=9, matching the handoff's own ~8 estimate within its stated margin).
leak_count.after: 7 genuinely-hanging live wasmex calls (call_timeout_test.exs: AC2 = 1, AC5's remaining live test = 1, total 2; plugin_handler_test.exs: REQ-165's own AC5 = 1 [untouched, out of scope -- different, already-shipped requirement], REQ-170 AC1 = 1, REQ-170 AC3 = 1, REQ-170 AC4 consolidated = 2, total 5; grand total 2+5=7).
leak_count.reduction: 9 -> 7 genuinely-hanging calls (~22% reduction). Every one of REQ-170's 7 real acceptance criteria (AC1-AC7, docs/requirements.yaml) still has at least one live, end-to-end test proving the real mechanism -- this hard constraint from the handoff's own AC1 was prioritized over chasing the 'roughly half' target number once every AC's live proof was already at its structural minimum (each remaining live call proves a distinct mechanism that cannot be made synthetic without losing real coverage of that AC). REQ-170's own test count went from 30 to 29 (one test removed by the AC4 consolidation).
